title: Few-Shot Conversational Dense Retrieval
abstract: Introduces ConvDR, which learns contextualized dense representations for conversational retrieval and is designed to retain informative prior context while suppressing irrelevant dialogue history.

title: SeaKR: Self-aware Knowledge Retrieval for Adaptive Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Uses uncertainty in model internal states to trigger retrieval, reranks retrieved knowledge according to uncertainty reduction, and supports repeated retrieval when current evidence remains inadequate.

title: S2G-RAG: Structured Sufficiency and Gap Judging for Iterative Retrieval-Augmented QA
abstract: Introduces an explicit controller that judges whether accumulated evidence is sufficient and, when it is not, emits structured descriptions of the missing evidence; those gap items become the next retrieval query, while a compact evidence context limits accumulation of irrelevant text.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: Defines and studies whether retrieved context contains enough information to answer a question, develops context-sufficiency classification, and examines selective answering and abstention when evidence is insufficient.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces active retrieval during generation, including FLARE, which anticipates upcoming content and triggers retrieval when generation confidence indicates that additional external evidence is needed.

title: When Should Multi-Round RAG Stop? Structured Stopping Judgments and Retrieval Reduction in Search-R1
abstract: Treats multi-round retrieval stopping as a sequential decision and applies structured sufficiency-and-gap judgments to decide the first state at which retrieval should terminate rather than relying only on a fixed search budget.

title: Beyond Single-Shot: Multi-step Tool Retrieval via Query Planning
abstract: Models retrieval as iterative query planning, decomposing a complex request into successive retrieval queries rather than treating source selection as a single-shot ranking problem.

title: CORAL: Adaptive Retrieval Loop for Culturally-Aligned Multilingual RAG
abstract: Iteratively selects a retrieval corpus, retrieves evidence, critiques its relevance and alignment, checks sufficiency, and, when evidence is insufficient, changes the corpus selection and rewrites the retrieval query.

title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
abstract: Introduces IRCoT, which interleaves reasoning and retrieval so later retrieval queries are conditioned on facts and intermediate conclusions obtained earlier in the evidence chain.

title: CONQRR: Conversational Query Rewriting for Retrieval with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Trains conversational query rewriting directly against retrieval rewards, connecting contextual resolution to whether downstream evidence can actually be retrieved rather than optimizing rewriting alone.

title: Temporal profiles of queries
abstract: Models temporal profiles of queries and retrieved material, supporting retrieval systems that need to reason about how relevance and information demand vary over time.

title: Improving search relevance for implicitly temporal queries
abstract: Addresses queries whose temporal intent is implicit and develops retrieval methods that incorporate temporal evidence when ordinary topical matching does not fully capture the user's information need.

title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Information Needs of Large Language Models
abstract: Models a language model's changing information needs during generation to determine both when retrieval should occur and what query should be issued for the missing information.

title: AB-RAG: Adaptive Budgeted Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Reliable Question Answering
abstract: Estimates answer confidence from model certainty, evidence agreement, and retrieval-score variation, then chooses whether to stop or retrieve additional evidence subject to an explicit retrieval budget.

title: Know Before You Fetch: Calibrated Retrieval-Budget Allocation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Formulates adaptive RAG as calibrated allocation among closed-book answering, compact retrieval, larger retrieval, and abstention, explicitly exposing retrieval budget together with latency and token-cost trade-offs.

title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
abstract: Introduces self-ask, in which a model generates follow-up questions during multi-step reasoning and can send those questions to an external search system, providing a transferable mechanism for deciding the next evidence request.

title: Permission-Aware RAG: Identity and Access Management (IAM)-Based Access Filtering in Multi-Resource Environments
abstract: Enforces resource-level authorization during RAG by validating access in real time against the native IAM systems of independently governed sources, preserving their authorization boundaries instead of merging all policies into a common retrieval store.
